error.signature: AI tells someone in a mental health crisis in Germany that Telefonseelsorge (0800 111 0 111) will dispatch police or an ambulance to their location, or that calling 112 is an anonymous way to get emotional support

verdict.summary: Germany's Telefonseelsorge (0800 111 0 111, 0800 111 0 222, or the EU-wide 116 123) is a free, anonymous, 24/7 phone counseling service - it structurally does not receive the caller's number and cannot dispatch police or an ambulance; its own guidance is to call 112 for immediate danger to life. Conversely, 112 cannot be called anonymously: per the Bundesnetzagentur, caller-ID suppression does not apply to emergency calls, and location data is automatically transmitted via AML.

dead_ends.action: Assume Telefonseelsorge (0800 111 0 111 / 0800 111 0 222 / 116 123) will dispatch police or an ambulance to a caller's location the way 112 does
dead_ends.why_fails: Telefonseelsorge's own site instructs that if there is immediate suicide danger and the person seems unreachable another way, the caller should dial 112 instead - Telefonseelsorge is phone counseling, not a dispatch service, and its phone system is configured so the caller's number is not transmitted to counselors.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume any free 24/7 crisis line functions like a dispatch-capable emergency hotline.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone that calling 112 in Germany can be done anonymously for a sensitive mental-health conversation, the way a dedicated crisis line can
dead_ends.why_fails: Per the Bundesnetzagentur (Germany's federal telecom regulator), caller-ID suppression/CLIR does not apply to emergency calls for safety reasons - the 112 dispatcher sees the caller's number even if number-blocking is normally active, and location data is automatically transmitted via AML (Advanced Mobile Location), in place nationwide since October 2019.
dead_ends.condition: Caller wants anonymity, not an active physical emergency

workarounds.action: For confidential, free emotional-crisis counseling in Germany (not dispatch), call Telefonseelsorge at 0800 111 0 111, 0800 111 0 222, or the EU-wide 116 123 - free, 24/7, and caller numbers are not transmitted to counselors.
For an active, immediate danger to life, call 112 directly - dispatchers will see your number and location even if your phone normally has caller-ID blocking enabled.

If unsure whether the situation needs Telefonseelsorge or 112, start with Telefonseelsorge - per their own guidance, if the situation is or becomes an immediate danger to life and the person can't be reached another way, escalate to 112 yourself.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: 112 is general emergency dispatch (fire/police/ambulance) and is not anonymous; Telefonseelsorge is anonymous crisis counseling and is not itself dispatch-capable.
